title: Harden setup, sessions and filesystem boundaries
goal: Review the alpha trust boundaries before any internet-facing deployment.
acceptance: Add adversarial setup-race, expired-cookie replay and progress-isolation tests.
Investigate no-follow file handles to eliminate filesystem swap races where supported.
Document password recovery and setup-token lifecycle; add tested credential-change session revocation.
Review rate limits, host filtering, CSRF and codec-process isolation with both maintainers.

title: Verify native distributions, container licensing and reproducible alpha builds
goal: Make Windows/Linux distributions independently runnable and review redistribution obligations.
acceptance: Smoke-test packaged UI, setup, FFprobe discovery and range playback on clean Windows/Linux machines.
Generate SBOM, checksums and third-party license inventory including container FFmpeg sources/build configuration.
Pin base images by digest and document toolchain pinning and artifact signing.
Exercise draft prerelease workflow and install/rollback instructions; do not publish stable.

title: Expose useful playback errors and streaming diagnostics
goal: Give users enough information to diagnose Direct Play without exposing private paths.
acceptance: Show client browser capabilities, selected codecs/container and chosen playback mode.
Return correlation IDs for probe/scan failures and sanitized per-file reasons to admins.
Show stream throughput and buffering indicators using browser metrics.
Add API and browser coverage for missing files, corrupt media and unsupported codecs.

title: Add bounded software transcoding and HLS sessions
goal: Implement the first fallback when Direct Play is unsupported.
acceptance: Plan direct/remux/transcode through IPlaybackPlanner and a new session abstraction.
Use argument lists, per-session cache directories, cancellation, process/time/disk quotas and cleanup.
Generate playable HLS with authentication on manifest and every segment.
Use synthetic fixtures to verify seeking, disconnect cleanup and concurrent session limits.

title: Add adaptive bitrate and network-aware quality selection
goal: Make HLS adapt to varying bandwidth.
acceptance: Offer a documented HLS rendition ladder and manual quality override.
Measure switching and rebuffering under throttled bandwidth.
Avoid duplicate encodes where compatible sessions can safely reuse cache.

title: Implement NVIDIA NVENC acceleration with safe fallback
goal: Provide a capability-driven NVIDIA transcoding adapter.
acceptance: Detect driver/device and codec support at runtime.
Select NVENC only when available and authorized; fall back to software.
Document container device access and driver compatibility.
Record encode performance and test unsupported-device behavior.

title: Implement Intel and AMD hardware acceleration adapters
goal: Support Intel QSV/VAAPI and AMD acceleration without vendor-specific core APIs.
acceptance: Define reusable capability discovery and device selection contracts.
Implement and document Linux VAAPI/Intel QSV and applicable Windows paths.
Provide explicit fallback and clear missing-driver diagnostics.
Publish hardware validation matrix with devices actually tested.

title: Validate AV1, HEVC, HDR and tone-mapping compatibility
goal: Produce correct playback plans across modern formats and displays.
acceptance: Probe bit depth, color primaries, transfer function and HDR metadata.
Build AV1/HEVC browser and hardware support matrix using licensed/synthetic fixtures.
Choose passthrough versus SDR conversion explicitly; never silently wash out HDR.
Benchmark tone mapping and preserve color/subtitle behavior.

title: Add subtitle and audio-track selection
goal: Let users choose accessible subtitles and the correct audio track.
acceptance: Expose complete track metadata and language labels.
Support browser-compatible external/embedded captions with authorization.
Switch audio safely and use remux/transcode when needed.
Sanitize rendered subtitle content and test keyboard/screen-reader selection.

title: Add movie and TV identification with cached artwork
goal: Organize filenames into real movie/series metadata without requiring cloud accounts.
acceptance: Use pluggable opt-in providers with operator-supplied keys stored outside the frontend.
Add local NFO/artwork support, explicit matching and manual correction.
Cache posters/backdrops with size limits, safe MIME handling and download host restrictions.
Respect provider rate limits, attribution and API terms; preserve offline behavior.

title: Add library monitoring, reconciliation and multiple library types
goal: Extend the existing multiple-directory model into reliable movie/TV libraries.
acceptance: Debounce filesystem events and reconcile moved/deleted files without deleting originals.
Provide separate movie/TV library types and per-library settings.
Detect duplicate files and expose suggested cleanup without destructive automation.
Recover from watcher overflow and inaccessible roots with observable jobs.

title: Add indexed search and smart collections
goal: Keep browsing responsive beyond small collections.
acceptance: Move search/filter/sort and cursor pagination to the API with bounded queries.
Add saved collection rules using validated typed filters.
Measure a synthetic 100k-item library and document latency targets.

title: Add multi-user administration, permissions and parental controls
goal: Build account management on the existing per-user progress and role model.
acceptance: Allow admins to create/disable accounts and reset passwords without exposing hashes.
Enforce library permissions and parental/content restrictions on every metadata and stream endpoint.
Persist watch history independently of resume state with tested user isolation.
Add session/device list and remote revocation; retain local-first operation.

title: Add watchlists, local recommendations and UI personalization
goal: Improve discovery without behavioral telemetry.
acceptance: Support per-user watchlists and deterministic local recommendation explanations.
Provide theme preferences and reduced-motion-aware animations.
Add configurable keyboard shortcuts that do not hijack form inputs.
Test touch and TV-style directional navigation.

title: Audit setup, library and player accessibility
goal: Establish measurable accessibility quality on real user flows.
acceptance: Run automated accessibility checks on setup/login/library/player/settings.
Manually verify keyboard focus, announcements, contrast and video controls.
Add targeted regressions for each confirmed defect and document browser limitations.

title: Implement authenticated playback handoff between devices
goal: Resume a current stream on a second authorized client.
acceptance: Use expiring single-use handoff requests, never raw media-path URLs.
Enforce user/device permissions and opt-in confirmation on destination.
Transfer position and selected tracks, handle stale/offline devices and avoid duplicate playback.

title: Define client SDK and ship a first Windows desktop client
goal: Establish a stable client contract before proliferating platform wrappers.
acceptance: Generate typed API contracts and document auth/range/HLS behavior.
Choose and justify Windows native playback integration versus an embedded browser.
Package a signed-installation-ready alpha and run a real stream against the server.
Document capability negotiation for subsequent mobile/TV clients.

title: Build Android, Android TV and Smart TV client foundations
goal: Expand to living-room devices after the client API is stable.
acceptance: Implement one Android playback/auth library shared with an Android TV shell.
Test remote-control focus, subtitle selection and capability reporting on actual devices.
Evaluate Smart TV targets individually with a compatibility matrix and explicit unsupported platforms.
Use CI-produced runnable packages and never claim an untested TV is supported.

title: Design and validate secure remote streaming
goal: Support optional remote access without exposing unsafe defaults.
acceptance: Document VPN-first setup and a tested TLS reverse-proxy reference configuration.
Trust forwarded headers only from explicit proxy addresses and preserve login/range/HLS/WebSocket semantics.
Add external URL validation, secure cookie checks and deployment readiness warnings.
Keep cloud accounts and public listeners optional.

title: Define a permissioned plugin API and example extension
goal: Allow extensions without silently granting arbitrary access to media and credentials.
acceptance: Write an ADR covering trust model, process isolation, capabilities and API versioning.
Implement one narrow metadata-provider example with explicit permissions.
Support disabling/recovering from a faulty plugin and report compatibility.
Never load unsigned/untrusted code automatically.

title: Add resource, active-stream and storage monitoring
goal: Make server load and media pipeline costs visible to administrators.
acceptance: Expose CPU/memory/storage statistics with platform-specific unavailable values clearly labeled.
Show authenticated active streams and transcoding rates/queue counts.
Add optional GPU metrics only on supported vendor adapters.
Test that ordinary users cannot see other users, device IDs or private paths.

title: Implement consistent backups, safe updates and rollback
goal: Make upgrades recoverable without risking personal media.
acceptance: Create consistent SQLite/key-ring/configuration backups with integrity checks and permissions.
Implement restore dry-run and documented migration compatibility gates.
Stage versioned binaries and require successful health/playback checks before switching.
Test failed migration and interrupted update rollback against copies of fixture data.
